title: SDK Orientation: Fasttrack Labs Roadmap
content:
Purpose
This doc outlines a compact, hands-on SDK orientation path (Fasttrack Labs) designed to get engineers from zero to a stable instrumented prototype in 50 requests or less. The goal is low-friction, observable progress: a reproducible lab that demonstrates generation, streaming, error handling, and telemetry hooks so teams can judge fit quickly.

Audience
- New SDK adopters (engineers/ML engineers) who want a quick proof-of-concept
- Solutions engineers running onboarding sessions
- Internal workshop leads for 30–90 minute demos

High-level constraints and principles
- Keep each lab <= 15 minutes (most ~6–12m).
- Minimal config: one env var (REDWOOD_API_KEY) and a tiny sample app.
- Telemetry wired by default (sane defaults: request_id, model, tokens_in/out, latency_ms).
- Failure-first checks: every step has one 'what-to-check' and one 'if-it-fails' remediation.
- Reproducible locally and in a sandboxed cloud workspace.

Learning objectives (what people can do by the end)
- Make a simple generation call and stream partial tokens into the UI.
- Swap model variants (dev -> cost) using the same API surface.
- Record and view telemetry for a small request sample (50 reqs) and interpret cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Implement a basic fallback policy and test a simulated capacity failure.

Fasttrack Labs (sequence)
1) Lab 0: Quick prep (2–3m)
   - Check prerequisites (Node 18+, Python 3.11, git).
   - Export REDWOOD_API_KEY and clone repo: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk-starter.git
   - Smoke test: run ./scripts/healthcheck.sh (expected output: OK).
   - What-to-check: healthcheck OK. If it fails: check env, network, see GH-PR 482 notes.

2) Lab 1: Hello stream (6–8m)
   - Goal: call /v1/generate, enable streaming, render partial tokens.
   - Steps: copy sample client snippet (node) -> set model=redwood-1-small -> run -> watch tokens appear in terminal/UI.
   - Telemetry hooks: ensure request_id is logged, latency shows initial-chunk time.
   - Failure tip: if no stream appears, toggle max_tokens to 64 and retry.

3) Lab 2: Prompt templating + deterministic test (8–10m)
   - Goal: use a small prompt template with placeholders and validate outputs consistently over 5 seeds.
   - Steps: integrate tiny templating helper (templates/simple.js), run batch of 5 with deterministic params, capture embeddings for comparison.
   - What-to-check: stable output shape and no streaming errors. If it fails: lower temperature to 0.2.

4) Lab 3: Swap-and-measure (6m)
   - Goal: switch from dev model -> cost-optimized quantized model using same SDK call and compare latency/cost.
   - Steps: change model parameter -> run 10 requests -> open local telemetry dashboard from /telemetry/last-run.
   - Metrics: median latency, p95 latency, tokens per request, cost estimate per-token.
   - What-to-check: cost delta printed. If it fails: ensure model variant is available in catalog (see CONFLUENCE: model catalog link).

5) Lab 4: Fallback simulation and canary (10m)
   - Goal: implement a client-side fallback that retries to a fallback model/region on 5xx or capacity errors, and test it by toggling a simulated outage flag.
   - Steps: enable FAKE_OUTAGE=true (dev flag in sample app), send 10 concurrent requests, assert fallback path was used at least once.
   - Telemetry: tag requests with fallback_used=true.
   - Failure tip: if fallback never triggers, increase concurrency to 25 to hit capacity branch.

6) Lab 5: Telemetry deep-dive (8–12m)
   - Goal: from a 50-request sample, create a short report: latency distribution, top error types, prompt length vs tokens used.
   - Steps: run the sample runner -> export telemetry.json -> run analyze_telemetry.py -> open report.html.
   - Expected output: small dashboard with charts for median/p95, error heatmap, and one suggestion line from Optimize heuristics (e.g., reduce batch size or shorten context).
   - What-to-check: cost per token and anomalies detected. If it fails: run with --preserve-logs to see raw events.

Cheatmap: One-page runloop for first 50 requests
- Boot -> set API key -> healthcheck -> run Lab1 (stream) -> run Lab3 (swap) -> run Lab4 (fallback) -> collect telemetry -> analyze.
- Exit criteria: produced a streamed response, observed fallback once, and generated a telemetry report.

Telemetry contract (minimal)
- Required fields: request_id, user_agent, model, model_variant, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens, latency_ms, status_code, error_type (if any), fallback_used (bool).
- Sample event format: flat JSON line per request (we log locally to telemetry/).
- Retention note: for workshop keep only last_run.json in repo to avoid PHI; never log customer inputs in shared repos.

Gating and success criteria for pilot handoff
- Developer can reproduce a 50-request report locally.
- App includes telemetry with the required fields and a README for where to find the dashboard.
- Solutions engineer signs off (ticket DEVEXP-197) once pilot README and logs present.

Failure scenarios & mitigations (common)
- 401/403: invalid API key or scope. Mitigation: re-issue key from Console, ensure project has 'fasttrack' entitlement.
- Streaming stall: chunk buffer too big or network issue. Mitigation: reduce chunk_size in client and enable keepalive.
- Outage/no fallback: missing fallback model in catalog. Mitigation: add a stable fallback model to environment or reduce concurrency.

Workshop script (30m variant)
- 0–3m: Intro + goals
- 3–12m: Lab1 + Lab2 (live coding)
- 12–22m: Lab3 + Lab4 (swap & fallback)
- 22–30m: Lab5 report + next steps, Q&A

Next steps / backlog ideas
- Polished flashcard-style quickchecks for each lab (pass/fail one-liners).
- Add prebuilt cloud sandbox image for instant run (GCP/AWS dev credits).
- Small web UI that renders the runloop cheatmap and shows live telemetry during labs.
- Integrate with Console to auto-provision temporary API keys for workshop attendees (epic).

Open questions
- Do we want workshop artifacts to include small sample user data? (privacy implications)
- Should we include a separate lab for embeddings + similarity search in the Fasttrack core flow, or treat it as an add-on?

References and links
- Confluence curriculum backlog: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEVEXP/SDK+Curriculum+Backlog
- Starter repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter (branch: fasttrack-labs)
- Ticket for pilot signoff: JIRA DEVEXP-197
- Slack channel for hands-on help: #eng-devexp-onboard

Notes to self (short)
- Keep labs lean: remove any step that needs >2 shell commands.
- Ensure analyze_telemetry.py is copy-paste friendly and deps are pinned.
- Demo checklist: stream visible, fallback triggered, telemetry report generated.
